Guanabara Bay in Rio de Janeiro is a scenic expanse of water surrounded by green hills and modern buildings, a true gem of the city. It is Brazil’s second-largest bay, and its shores bring together history, culture and nature. Guanabara impresses with its beauty and variety: its waters wash famous beaches such as Copacabana and Ipanema, while the celebrated Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer statue rise on the horizon. The bay contains numerous islands, including well-known Paquetá Island, which can only be reached by boat.

Historically, Guanabara was an important trading and strategic center. Today it provides a beautiful setting for countless yachts and sailboats, creating an atmosphere of serenity and romance.

Boat and catamaran excursions on the bay are an excellent way to see Rio from an unusual perspective, enjoying magnificent views of the city and its surroundings. Guanabara Bay is both a natural wonder and a cultural symbol of Rio de Janeiro, something to experience to truly appreciate the magic of this remarkable city.

You depart Marina da Glória port aboard a comfortable vessel and enjoy views of one of Brazil’s largest and most beautiful bays. Sea breezes, blue ocean water and splendid scenery surround you.

During the excursion you will see some of Rio de Janeiro’s finest panoramas. Sail past the well-known neighborhoods of Botafogo, Flamengo and Urca. Even from a distance, Sugarloaf Mountain, the tropical islands, Fort São João and the Rio–Niterói Bridge are impressive, along with the Modern Art Museum building designed by Niemeyer, the sixteenth-century Santa Cruz Fortress and the favelas on the hillsides.

## Boat Trip on Guanabara Bay

A gentle sea breeze, panoramic views and a feeling of complete tranquility make this boat trip a magical way to see Rio from the water. As the boat glides across the bay, the view becomes a living postcard: majestic Sugarloaf Mountain, coastal fortresses, tropical islets and Niemeyer’s modern art museum with its elegant lines. Relax, breathe deeply and enjoy the peaceful beauty of one of Brazil’s most impressive bays.

Feel the ocean breeze and watch Rio de Janeiro shine as you cruise through historic, scenic Guanabara Bay.

From the deck, discover Rio’s beauty in motion: towering peaks, tropical forests and the lively waterfront of one of the world’s most captivating bays.

In Acajatuba Village, local residents engage in fishing and farming. They cultivate cassava and other plants that are part of everyday Amazonian life.

During a visit, you can learn about local customs, cassava flour preparation and handicrafts. Natural seeds are among the materials used to make crafts. The village is included in river itineraries departing from Manaus and the Rio Negro area.

The landscapes of Aconcagua are full of contrasts: arid mountain valleys and rocky slopes give way to snowy peaks, glaciers and deep gorges. In sunlight, the slopes take on golden and ocher tones, while clouds clinging to the peaks lend the mountain an almost otherworldly appearance.

The mountain stands within Aconcagua Provincial Park, established to protect its exceptional high-altitude landscapes and fragile ecosystem. Here you can see rare plants adapted to the harsh climate and encounter local wildlife, including guanacos and Andean condors.

Aconcagua draws mountaineers from around the world who dream of reaching one of the planet’s great summits. The climb, however, requires serious physical preparation, time for acclimatization and careful planning. For travelers not aiming for the top, the park offers hiking routes, walks through mountain valleys and opportunities to enjoy panoramic Andean views without a difficult ascent.

The road to Aconcagua is an experience in itself, passing through the high-altitude scenery of the Andes. Along the way, colorful rock formations, snow-covered ranges and broad valleys reveal the immense scale of the natural landscape.

Aconcagua embodies the grandeur of the Andes in a single summit, a place where the earth rises toward the sky and every view across the mountains recalls the power of nature and the human desire to explore new horizons.
